rv.q: As gleefully as the musical follows the formula of the rom-com genre, it also has a welcome comfort with ambiguity and, stashed up its sleeve, some psychological bombs.
A modest but charming musical rom-com from the UK plucks at the heart, and the players are the main reason New York and points west should keep an eye out for this sparkling two-hander.
It is an act of prestidigitation: Entertainment and real emotional engagement are pulled out of thin air.
What ultimately makes Two Strangers such a winning Broadway arrival is its belief that tenderness is still theatrical currency.
This is a charming little show (which definitely doesn't need to be two hours and twenty minutes long)
Like a Hallmark movie, “Two Strangers” boasts enough humor and whimsy to be sweet and superficially appealing, but at the end, all we’re left with is the superficial.

cn.t: Critics warmly embrace this charming romantic musical, praising its tender sincerity and the winning chemistry of leads Sam Tutty and Christiani Pitts, who carry the modest two-hander with skill and heart.
